19e73fdeb008: Trap: pies and kot are masculine, but they are animals, so [[te]] psy, [[te]] koty. The «ci» group is only for male people.
1e3a518032ab: How to find the ending: remove the singular ending (-a) and look at the last consonant. A hard consonant — b, p, f, w, m, n, t, d, s, z, ł, r — gives [[-y]]. After k and g it is always [[-i]], because Polish has no «ky» or «gy».
7484c36dcf50: The plural of książka is książk[[i]]. After k and g we never write -y.
c5730ae5d232: [[-e]] is taken by masculine and feminine nouns whose stem ends in: a soft consonant ń, ś, ź, ć, dź (before a vowel we write [[ni, si, zi, ci, dzi]]), l, j, or c, cz, sz, rz, ż, dż. Words in -ia, -ja belong here too: lekcja, historia, alergia.

a2d6e8c353dc: Don't mix them up: [[kuchnie]] — plural (te kuchnie są duże), while «kuchni» — genitive singular (nie ma kuchni). The same: [[lekcje]] ≠ lekcji.
36aa6376de28: In the plural the word gets one syllable longer, and the vowel in the last syllable often changes. Learn such pairs together: [[stół — stoły]].
0c2e586e6418: Not every ó alternates: góra → góry, ogórek → ogórki. If you are not sure, check a dictionary.
5b6e554733e5: In the te group it is not only the noun that changes. The pronoun → [[te, moje, nasze]], the adjective → [[-e]], the verb in the past tense → [[-ły]].
